Photograph: Adam Gray/Reuters E Jean Carroll US supreme court again rejects Trump’s bid to overturn E Jean Carroll verdict Decision leaves intact $5m civil judgment against Trump after jury found him liable for sexually abusing writer Anna Betts Mon 17 Aug 2026 12.49 EDT First published on Mon 17 Aug 2026 11.35 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The US supreme court has rejected for a second time Donald Trump’s attempt to overturn a jury verdict in 2023 that found him liable for sexually ​abusing writer E Jean Carroll , and later defaming her. The court announced the decision in an unsigned order on Monday, without providing an explanation of their decision. The order just listed the US president’s petition, along with several other petitions, under “rehearings denied”. Roberta Kaplan, Carroll’s attorney, said: “We are pleased that the United States supreme court has declined again to hear this case. As a result, the jury’s unanimous verdict that Donald Trump sexually assaulted and then defamed E Jean Carroll is now final and cannot be challenged in any court.” In 2025, Trump – who has repeatedly denied Carroll’s allegations against him – asked the supreme court to review the case in 2025 and overturn the verdict. Carroll’s lawyers urged the justices to reject his petition and in June of this year, the supreme court declined to hear Trump’s appeal. His lawyers then asked the justices to reconsider. The decision on Monday leaves intact the $5m civil judgment against Trump, that was returned by the jury after the two-week trial in 2023. Trump had deposited this $5m jury award, along with interest, into a court-held account several weeks after the verdict. And in July, after the supreme court first declined Trump’s attempt to appeal the verdict, a Manhattan federal judge ordered that the funds be released and Carroll’s legal team said that the money, totaling about $5.6m, had been disbursed to her. In 2024 , a three-judge court panel at the second US circuit court of appeals in Manhattan also upheld the jury’s verdict. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Monday about the supreme court’s decision. Carroll also brought a separate defamation suit against Trump in 2024, a separate federal jury ordered Trump to pay Carroll $83.3m in damages after concluding that he had defamed her in 2019. Trump’s lawyers are appealing that ruling to the supreme court. And according to NBC News , the court is not set to act on that appeal until later this year. Last September, a federal appeals court upheld the $83.3m jury award. Photograph: Stéphanie Lecocq/Reuters France Macron condemns racism after one killed in ‘terrorist’ shooting near Paris Gunman opens fire from car in Trappes and Verrière, killing one and injuring five others, including a 12-year-old girl Angelique Chrisafis in Paris Fri 23 Oct 2026 15.23 EDT Last modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 15.44 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Emmanuel Macron has condemned racism in French society after a gunman opened fire from a car west of Paris on Friday, killing one person, wounding a 12-year-old girl and injuring four others in what the president called a “racist terrorist attack”. Macron arrived at the scene of the drive-by shooting in Trappes, a town west of Paris, on Friday night, saying he was deeply saddened by what he called the “premeditated” attack. The 12-year-old girl, who was shot eight times, is being treated in hospital. “What happened today ​marks a turning point for our ⁠country; what happened today ​was ​a terrorist ​and racist attack,” ​Macron said. He said the gunman had targeted people because of the colour of their skin. The president said racism had often become part of the “ambient discourse in France” and created “an atmosphere”. He said: “Don’t let this terrorist attack divide us.” He called for “respect and unity”, saying many French people would be scared and thinking “this could happen to me”. Ali Rabeh, the leftwing mayor of Trappes, said that the gunman had set out by car on Friday morning “firing at random, wanting to cause a bloodbath” as he drove through the town and neighbouring La Verrière. The mayor called it “objectively a racist attack, probably Islamophobic”. Rabeh, whose family has Moroccan roots, said: “The people targeted today could just as easily have been my mother, my brothers or my sisters-in-law. “A 12-year-old girl is between life and death after being targeted by a volley of automatic gunfire in our country. Her crime was probably being of colour,” he added. “It’s probably one of the first attempts at a mass crime of Islamophobia and racism.” Rabeh said everyone in France had a responsibility to bring “calm and harmony”. He called for a collective condemnation of rhetoric that “ideologically arms those capable of carrying out such acts”. Anti-terrorism prosecutors are investigating whether the gunman targeted the “real or supposed race, ethnicity, nationality or religion” of the victims. The 39-year-old suspect, who was stopped by police in his car, was named by France’s anti-terrorism prosecutor as Kevin T. He had driven through the towns of Trappes and La Verrière in Yvelines at about 10.30am on Friday. Over the course of 15 minutes, he repeatedly fired an automatic weapon, first at a petrol station, then a medical centre and a children’s playground. The French public broadcaster reported that he shot dead a young black man, then targeted a woman wearing a headscarf, before shooting the 12-year-old girl, who was being treated for her eight gunshot wounds at a children’s hospital on Friday night. The prosecutor said in a statement on Friday night that the medical status of the five wounded victims was not stable. Rabeh said the man killed was “of African origin” and that another of the wounded was “of north African origin”. Nicolas Dainville, the mayor of La Verrière, told Agence France-Presse that two of the wounded people in his town were cleaners of African origin attending to a school Friday on morning when the shooter got out of his car to open fire. The prosecutor said that when the suspect was stopped by police in his car he was found with a sten gun – a British submachine gun used in the second world war – as well as teargas grenades. The man had also booby-trapped his home with gas canisters and electric wires connected to a timer, authorities said, adding that a member of his family was arrested and taken into custody for questioning. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to This is Europe The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment after newsletter promotion “The investigations are ongoing, but it is clearly a terrorist crime. It is an extremely serious act,” the interior minister, Laurent Nunez, told reporters from ⁠Yvelines. The ‌shooting comes at a moment of particular tension in France. Last Saturday saw one of the most violent days of unrest in years , which left public buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and looted, and at least 2,400 people arrested in cities across the country. Renewed protests, over teacher shortages and crumbling buildings in high schools as well as the high cost of living, are expected on Saturday. Marine Le Pen, the leader of the far-right anti-immigration the National Rally party, is polling highly ahead of next spring’s presidential election when Macron steps down. After the Trappes attack, Fabien Roussel, a Communist candidate, wrote on social media that the far right was responsible for “racist hatred” in France. Le Pen condemned what she called the “abject motive of racism” of the “barbaric act”. Photograph: Cillian Sherlock/Press Association Tom Tuite Tue Oct 27 2026 - 20:52 • 2 MIN READ A 47-year-old man has been remanded in custody charged with the murder of his partner in Finglas, Dublin . Loredana Morosanu (48) was discovered fatally injured in her home at Melville Terrace, Finglas, in the early hours of Monday. Emergency services were called to the house at 4.30am and found her. The pharmacy worker, who was originally from Romania but had lived in Ireland for several years, was pronounced dead at the scene. Gardaí arrested Daniel Simion Toader, also of Melville Terrace, and charged him on Tuesday evening with the murder of Loredana Morosanu at their home address on October 26th, contrary to common law. READ MORE David Walliams accused by multiple people of using celebrity status to prey on young women for sex Former US president Joe Biden makes surprise appearance in Dublin Republicans ran their campaign like a Conor McGregor press conference Leinster released 30 players to their clubs and the AIL came alive The Romanian national appeared before Judge Máire Conneely at a late special sitting of Dublin District Court at about 8:20pm. Loredana Morosanu, whose body was found at a house in Finglas on Sunday morning Dressed in a blue sweater, grey tracksuit bottoms and black shoes, he stood with his hands in his pockets at the start of the two-minute hearing. He then sat and spoke only to a court-appointed interpreter. He had no legal representation in court. Most criminal law solicitors in Dublin have withdrawn their services in response to legal aid payment reforms introduced in July, causing widespread disruption to the criminal justice system. Det Sgt Niall Murray told the judge that Toader was arrested at 6.58pm on Tuesday and made “no reply” when charged just under an hour later. Murray explained that the accused had eight consultations with a solicitor while in Garda custody, as well as one consultation just before coming to court. The court heard that the circumstances of being charged, along with his situation and the consequences regarding bail, had been explained to him “at length”. The District Court does not have jurisdiction to grant bail in a murder charge, which requires an application to the High Court . The judge noted that the issue of bail did not arise and remanded Toader in custody to appear at Cloverhill District Court on November 3rd via video-link.
